headlines.headline: Michigan Democrat crosses party lines
headlines.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, publicly endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Nov. 1 — the most unusual case of intra-party defection in a top-tier Senate race this cycle, following days of public friction over an ad Stevens called antisemitic.

headlines.headline: Five Senate toss-ups, Cruz's warning
headlines.summary: CBS's data desk rates Maine, Michigan, Ohio, Texas and Alaska as Senate toss-ups and newly moved South Carolina to lean-R after a tied NYT/Siena poll. Sen. Ted Cruz publicly warned Republicans could lose Texas and both chambers if conservative turnout lags.

headlines.headline: Trump, Obama trade closing arguments
headlines.summary: Dueling rallies in Georgia and Ohio in the campaign's final days: Obama framed the Iran war's cost to consumers campaigning for Sen. Jon Ossoff, while Trump defended his foreign-policy record campaigning for Ohio's Vivek Ramaswamy.

headlines.headline: Alaska "two Sullivans" suit dismissed
headlines.summary: A federal judge dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska's Senate race over a second, same-named candidate on the ballot, ruling the government lacked standing. A separate DOJ criminal probe continues.

headlines.outlet: University of Florida Election Lab (via CBS)
headlines.headline: Early voting tops 49.6 million
headlines.summary: Roughly 49.6 million early votes had been cast nationally as of the final weekend before Election Day — a marker of unusually high engagement heading into Nov. 3.

podcasts.summary: "Three Days Until the Midterms. How Bad Could It Get for Republicans?" (Nov 1) — Bill Kristol and Sarah Longwell on disillusioned Trump voters in her focus groups, Democratic openings in red states, and live reaction to the Stevens/Rogers endorsement.
"Can I trust the polls? And other questions from listeners about the 2026 midterms" (Oct 31) — NPR's politics team answers listener questions on polling reliability heading into Election Day.

"Have Republicans Already Blown the Midterms?" (Oct 18) — Dan Pfeiffer interviews Cook Political Report's Amy Walter on whether redistricting backfired on the GOP and whether the numbers show a Democratic wave.

wildcard: A federal judge dismissed a Trump DOJ lawsuit that sought to block certification of Alaska's Senate race over a second candidate who happens to share Sen. Dan Sullivan's exact name — one of the stranger ballot disputes of the cycle, with a separate criminal probe still open.
